newsitem.title: CROATIA: Croat Zagrebacka Banka says deposits, loans rising.
newsitem.headline: Croat Zagrebacka Banka says deposits, loans rising.

text.p: Leading Croatian commercial bank Zagrebacka Banka said on Thursday all deposits were up sharply in the first nine months this year, allowing it to further increase loans to its clients.
"This does not mean we want to support consumption but real investments, and our interest rates reflect this," retail banking director Zvonimir Jurjevic told reporters.
Kuna savings jumped 53 percent to 175 million kuna at the end of September and their term structure improved to 53 percent in favour of longer deposits, he said.
Foreign exchange savings rose by 342 million German marks or 32 percent to 1.43 billion marks, of which 61 percent are term deposits.
In this period the bank considerably boosted loans, with those to citizens alone totalling 195 million marks, rising 37 percent from the end of last year.
Jurjevic said the bank would continue to help businesses and citizens with credits such as those for the purchase of housing, now granted at a fixed interest rate of nine percent.
It would keep the highest interest of 9-11 percent a year on short- and medium-term cash loans for general purposes or a variable 8.0 percent charged for imported cars.
Zagrebacka decided to trim kuna lending rates by one percentage point to between 16 and 20 percent from November 1 and deposit rates by 0.5-1 point depending on term.
"It may seem modest but our charges are also to be halved to 0.5 percent, which is a big cut," Jurjevic said.

As a first step to raising cheaper foreign capital that would enable it to further cut interest rates, the bank asked for a credit rating from three leading international agencies earlier this month. -- Kolumbina Bencevic, Zagreb Newsroom, 385-1-4557075
